newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish police quell bloody prison riot.
newsitem.headline: Turkish police quell bloody prison riot.

text.p: Baton-wielding gendarmerie police on Wednesday quelled a riot at a Turkish prison that killed up to eight people.
"The information I have received shows that there are eight dead and 11 injured," an Istanbul health board official told Reuters.
But Anatolian news agency quoted Justice Minister Oltan Sungurlu as saying that only five prisoners had died in the riot, over conditions and alleged maltreatment at Metris prison.
The jail holds 1,200 people despite being built for only 700 inmates.
A cordon of police stood guard around the jail in a rundown section of the city after the disturbance ended. Two buses full of police reinforcements and an armoured car waited nearby.
Gendarmerie police stormed the jail early in the morning and seized control of it from inmates who had taken a warden hostage and lit fires in cells on Tuesday night.
Anxious relatives gathered outside the prison. "We haven't been told anything," said Murat Anci, whose prisoner son was inside. Another relative fainted from the heat and stress.
Turkish television showed pictures of gendarmes beating inmates with batons and rifle butts and forcing them into a prison van after the riot ended.
Anatolian said the cause of the riot was the stabbing to death of an inmate on Monday night. The rioters were jailed for criminal offences and had no political demands, the agency said.
"I listened to their requests. They said they wanted better treatment and conditions," Anatolian quoted Istanbul governor Ridvan Yenisen as saying after visiting the prison.
